kpis.note: $3.16B — a quarterly record; $10.03B for the full year

otherDetail: Non-operating items added $3M: $57M of other income and $12M of investment gains, less $66M of interest expense.
pngFooterNote: Revenue is split by type, not by customer group.

segments.name: Subscription
segments.note: Creative Cloud, Acrobat and Experience Cloud subscriptions — 97 cents of every revenue dollar. Creative & Marketing Professionals paid $4,250M (+11%); Business Professionals & Consumers paid $1,720M (+15%).

segments.name: Product
segments.note: One-time software licenses — a small legacy line from before Adobe moved to subscriptions.

segments.name: Services and other
segments.note: Consulting, training and support services sold alongside the software.

takeaways.text: Revenue hit a record $6,194M, up 10% (10% in constant currency), and GAAP net income rose to $1,856M, up 10% year over year. For the full fiscal year, revenue was $23.77B, up 11%, and remaining performance obligations — work customers have already committed to — stood at $22.52B.
takeaways.title: A record quarter to close a record year

takeaways.text: Subscription revenue grew 12% to $5.99B, and total ARR reached $25.20B at year end, up 11.5%. Business Professionals & Consumers subscription revenue grew 15% to $1.72B, faster than the creative professional line's 11% to $4.25B.
takeaways.title: Subscriptions keep compounding

takeaways.text: Operating cash flow was a quarterly record $3.16B — more than the quarter's $1.86B of net income, because customers pay for subscriptions up front. Adobe also repurchased 7.2 million shares in the quarter, 30.8 million for the full year.
takeaways.title: Cash flow hit a record too

verdict: Adobe closed FY2025 with record quarterly revenue of $6.19B, up 10%, and record operating cash flow of $3.16B, as subscriptions grew 12% and total ARR reached $25.20B.
